title: Controlling Particle Fraction in Microporous Annealed Particle Scaffolds for 3D Cell Culture
protocol: Mix polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) elastomer base with the curing agent at a 10:1 ratio.
Prepare approximately 100 g of PDMS mixture to cover the wafer with ~5 mm thickness.
Pour the PDMS mixture onto the wafer and degas in a desiccator for about 30 min.
Place the PDMS-covered wafer in an oven at 60 °C for at least 2 h to cure the PDMS.
Gently trace around the parameter of the device on the wafer with a knife without cracking it.
Carefully peel the cured PDMS off the wafer.
Use a 1 mm biopsy punch to create inlet and outlet channels in the PDMS device.
Remove dust from the feature side of the device using tape gently.
Place the devices and clean glass slides on a hot plate at 135 °C for at least 15 min to remove moisture.
Weigh the reactants for HA-norbornene synthesis.
Dissolve 20 mg/mL hyaluronic acid (HA) in 200 mM MES buffer (pH ~6).
Add DMTMM to the HA solution and allow it to react at room temperature for approximately 20 min.
Add NMA dropwise to the HA/DMTMM solution under stirring.
Cover the reaction vessel with foil and continue stirring while allowing the reaction to proceed for approximately 24 h.
Chill ethanol (approximately 10x the reaction volume) in preparation for precipitating HA-NB.
Transfer the reaction dropwise to chilled ethanol on a stir plate to precipitate HA-NB.
Continue stirring at 200-300 rpm for 20 min after transferring the solution to ethanol.
Transfer the solution to 50 mL conical tubes.
Centrifuge at 5,000 x g for 10 min.
Pour off excess ethanol as waste.
Pull vacuum on the HA-NB in a dessicator to dry overnight.
Purify the HA-NB using 12-14 kDa molecular weight cut-off cellulose dialysis tubing.
Dissolve HA-NB in 2 M NaCl solution and transfer to the dialysis tubing.
Tie the tubing and secure with clamps if needed.
Transfer the filled dialysis tubing to a bucket with 5 L of ultrapure water.
Dialyze the HA-NB against water overnight.
Remove the water from the bucket after dialysis and replace with 1 M NaCl solution for 30 min.
Remove the NaCl solution and then dialyze against ultrapure water for 3 days, replacing the water daily.
Filter the dialyzed product using a 0.2 µm vacuum-driven filter.
Transfer the filtered product to 50 mL conical tubes.
Add liquid nitrogen to a cryogenic container and flash-freeze the HA-NB tubes for 10 min.
Remove the conical tubes with forceps and quickly remove the cap.
Cover the conical tube with lab-grade tissue and secure it with a rubber band.
Transfer the covered conical tube to a lyophilization container or chamber.
Lyophilize the product.
Store the lyophilized HA-NB at -20 °C.
Dissolve HA-NB at 10 mg/mL in D2O.
Analyze the dissolved HA-NB via proton NMR.
Calibrate the D2O solvent peak to 4.8 PPM.
Integrate the peak for the HA methyl protons (δ2.05) and calibrate integration to 3.0.
Integrate the peaks for the pendant norbornene groups at δ6.33 and δ6.02.
Normalize the integration of these peaks to the corresponding number of protons to determine the average degree of modification.
Prepare 50 mM HEPES buffer (pH 7.5).
Sterilize filter the HEPES buffer using a 0.2 μm vacuum-driven filter.
Prepare respective 50 mM stocks of lithium phenyl(2,4,6,-trimethylbenzoyl)phosphinate (LAP) photo-initiator and tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP) reducing agent in the HEPES buffer.
Keep the LAP solution away from light.
Prepare respective 50 mM stocks of di-thiol linker and RGD peptide in sterile distilled water.
Weigh out HA-NB and dissolve in HEPES buffer to prepare a 10 mg/mL stock.

Combine the precursor components with final concentrations of 9.9 mM LAP, 0.9375 mM TCEP (4 thiol/TCEP), 2.8 mM di-thiol linker, 1 mM RGD peptide, and 3.5 wt% (w/v) HA-NB by adding extra HEPES buffer to reach the desired final volume.
Mix the precursor well using a positive displacement pipette.
Using a P1000 pipette, slowly pull up the entire mixture.
Put the tip onto the end of a 1 mL syringe and eject the tip from the pipette.
Pull the syringe plunger to load the mixture into the syringe.
Add a 0.2 μm filter on the end of syringe and filter into a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the filtered precursor solution to remove bubbles produced during filtering.
Using a P1000 pipette, slowly pull up the filtered precursor being careful not to create bubbles.
If there are bubbles, gently tap the tip for them to dislodge and float to the top.
Place the tip onto the end of a 1 mL syringe and eject the tip from the pipette.
Keep the syringe vertical and pull the syringe plunger slowly until the entire precursor solution is in the syringe.
Add a blunt tip needle to the syringe and push the precursor through the tip of the needle.
Wrap the syringe in foil to keep out of light.
Prepare 5% v/v Span-80 in heavy white mineral oil and mix well.
Desiccate to remove bubbles.
Keep the surfactant/oil mixture at room temperature wrapped in foil.
Mix well and desiccate prior to each use.
Use a 5 mL syringe to draw up the oil/surfactant mixture until the distance between the plunger and the fingerhold is approximately equal to the distance of the precursor syringe.
Add a blunt needle to the syringe and push the oil through the tip of the needle.
Add a blunt needle to a 1 mL syringe and fill with synthetic hydrophobic treatment solution.
Gently flow the solution through the microfluidic device until it pools at each inlet/outlet.
Let the solution dry in the device on the benchtop for approximately 30 min.
Pull vacuum on the outlet to remove excess solution.
Secure the device with clamps on a tabletop microscope.
Wrap a 15 mL conical tube with foil.
Place the wrapped conical tube in a tube rack as the microgel collection container.
Use a ring stand and clamp to position the UV light probe into the opening of the collection tube.
Measure the UV intensity using a UV detector, moving the probe until 20 mW/cm² is achieved.
Turn off the UV light.
Cut tubing to reach from the microfluidic device to the collection container.
Cut one end of the tubing at a 45° angle.
Gently insert the angled end of the tubing into the outlet channel.
Secure both precursor and oil phase syringes on a dual-syringe pump.
Cut two more pieces of tubing that will reach from syringe tips to the microfluidic device.
Cut one end of each tube at a 45° angle.
Carefully secure the tubing (blunt end) onto both syringe tips.
Adjust settings on the pump for the 1 mL syringe, including approximate precursor volume.
Slowly push the pump forward until enough pressure is applied to the syringe plungers to push oil and precursor through the tubing, removing air from the system.
Let the pressure equalize for 5-10 minutes.
Gently insert the angled end of the tubing into the inlet channels of the microfluidic device.
Place the microgel precursor solution in the front inlet and the pinching oil in the back inlet.
Move the pump forward in small increments until flow begins in the device.
Observe spherical microgels forming at the flow-focusing region.
Start the pump with a 0.4 µL/min flowrate.
Let the device run until it stabilizes.
Adjust the flow rate ±0.1 µL/min in small increments if needed to stabilize microgel production.
Replace the collection tube with a new tube once microgel production is stable.
Turn on the UV light after replacing the collection tube.
Check the run periodically to ensure microgel production remains stable over time.
Purify microgels.
Dry microgels.
Prepare microgel washing buffer using 300 mM HEPES, 50 mM NaCl, and 50 mM CaCl2.
Sterilize the washing buffer and Pluronic F-127 surfactant solution using a 0.2 µm vacuum-driven filter.
Centrifuge the microgel collection tube at 5,000 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant oil phase in a sterile hood.
Combine the microgels with Pluronic F-127 surfactant solution (1:1) and vortex to mix well.
Centrifuge the mixture at 5,000 x g for 5 min and aspirate the washing solution.
Add washing buffer at 4x volume of microgel and vortex to mix well.
Centrifuge the mixture at 5,000 x g for 5 min and aspirate the washing solution.
Repeat washes with washing buffer until no bubbles remain (4-8 washes).
Dissolve Alexa Fluor 488-Tet lyophilized product in dimethylformamide at 1 mg/mL and store at -20°C.
Prepare a working solution of Alexa Fluor 488-Tet by diluting the stock 1:14 in sterile PBS.
Combine the microgels with the working solution (2:1 by volume) in a sterile hood.
Use a displacement pipette and mix well.
Incubate the mixture for 1 h at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C.
Centrifuge the mixture at 5,000 x g.
Aspirate the staining solution.
Wash the µgels twice with 1x PBS (1:1 by volume).
Transfer purified µgels to a cryo-safe screw-cap tube using a displacement pipette.
Add 70% ethanol to the purified µgels at a ratio of 50% (v/v) and mix well with a displacement pipette.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 5,000 x g.
Aspirate the supernatant liquid.
Replace with 70% ethanol at a ratio of 50% v/v.
Mix well with a displacement pipette.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C.
Briefly centrifuge to ensure the µgels are at the bottom of the screw-cap tube.
Add liquid nitrogen to a cryogenic container, and then add the tube of µgels to flash-freeze.
After 5-10 min, remove the tube of µgels with forceps.
Quickly remove the cap and cover with a lab-grade tissue.
Secure the tissue with a rubber band and transfer to a lyophilization container or chamber.
Load the sample on the lyophilizer following the manufacturer's instructions.
Lyophilize at 0.066 Torr and -63 °C.
Store the lyophilized µgels (lyo-µgels) tightly sealed at room temperature.
Weigh the reactants.
Dissolve the HA at 20 mg/mL in 200 mM MES buffer (pH ~6) by stirring.
Add DMTMM to the HA solution and allow to react for approximately 20 min at room temperature.
Dissolve tetrazine-amine at 15 mg/mL in 200 mM MES buffer.
Add the tetrazine-amine dropwise to the HA/DMTMM solution.
Cover the reaction vessel with parafilm and aluminum foil.
Continue stirring for approximately 24 h at room temperature.
Chill ethanol (approximately 10x the reaction volume).
Transfer the reaction dropwise to the chilled ethanol to precipitate the HA-Tet.
Stir the mixture for 20 min on a stir plate.
Centrifuge the solution at 5,000 x g for 10 min.
Pour off the excess ethanol and dispose as waste.
Dry the HA-Tet in a dessicator under vacuum overnight.
Dissolve HA-Tet in 2 M NaCl solution.
Transfer the solution to cellulose dialysis tubing with a 12-14 kDa molecular weight cut-off.
Place the dialysis tubing in a bucket containing 5 L of ultrapure water.
Dialyze the HA-Tet against water overnight.
Remove the water and replace with 1 M NaCl solution for 30 min.
Remove the NaCl solution, then dialyze against ultrapure water for 3 days, replacing the water daily.
Filter the dialyzed product using a 0.2 µm vacuum-driven filter.
Transfer the filtered HA-Tet product to 50 mL conical tubes.
Flash-freeze the conical tubes in liquid nitrogen for 10 min.
Remove the flash-frozen conical tubes with forceps.
Quickly remove the cap and cover the conical tube with a lab-grade tissue.
Secure the tissue with a rubber band and transfer the conical tube to a lyophilization container or chamber.
Lyophilize the product.
Store the lyophilized product at -20°C.
Reconstitute lyo-µgels in 84% of the final MAP volume of 1x PBS.
Allow microgels to swell for approximately 20 minutes.
Dissolve HA-Tet in 1x PBS at the chosen concentration.
Combine the HA-Tet solution with the rehydrated lyo-µgels using a displacement pipette.
Mix well after combining the solutions.
Transfer the mixture onto glass slides, well plates, or another container of choice via displacement pipette.
Allow µgels to anneal at 37 °C for 25 minutes.
Use a spatula to transfer the MAP scaffolds to well plates filled with 1x PBS.
Keep MAP scaffolds in 1x PBS until ready for characterization.
Transfer MAP scaffold to a glass coverslip using a spatula.
Image MAP scaffolds on a confocal microscope with laser for FITC excitation and emission.
Obtain a Z-stack image of 250-300 µm in the Z-direction with a step size of 2.5 µm using a 20x objective.
Import the Z-stack image into analysis software.
Select the Add New Surfaces button in the analysis software.
Check the box to Segment Only a Region of Interest and select Next: Region of Interest.
Define a region of interest, noting the X-, Y-, and Z-dimensions of the volume being analyzed.
Use a minimum Z-height for the region of interest that includes at least two µgels.
Select the blue arrow button Next: Source Channel.
Use the drop-down list to select the FITC channel as the source channel.
Check the box next to Smooth and input a surface detail of 2.50 µm.
Under Thresholding, select Absolute Intensity and then select Next: Threshold.
Rotate the 3D projection to assess rendering quality and adjust if necessary.
Select Next: Classify Surfaces.
Check whether Number of Voxels is 10.0.
Select the green double arrow button Finish to execute all creation steps and terminate the wizard.
Select the Statistics tab, then the Detailed tab.
Use the second drop-down box to select the variable Volume.
Select the floppy disk button Export Statistics on Tab Display to File.
Save the exported data as a spreadsheet file (.xls).
Open the saved file.
Use the SUM function on Column A Volume to determine the total volume (µm³) of the µgels in the region of interest.
Convert the dimensions of the region of interest from pixels to µm using the µm/pixel calibration from step 4.3.1.
Multiply the Z-dimension (number of steps) by the step size for the image to convert the Z-dimension to µm.
Calculate the volume of the region of interest by multiplying the X-, Y-, and Z-dimensions.
Determine the particle fraction of the scaffold by dividing the total volume of the µgels in the region of interest by the volume of the region of interest.
Prepare cell culture devices using a 3D printer and the CAD file found in Supplemental Coding File 1.
Mix polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) elastomer base with the curing agent at a 10:1 ratio by mass.
Pour the PDMS mixture into a large plastic Petri dish and degas in a desiccator for approximately 30 min or until all the bubbles have disappeared.
Place the 3D printed mold into the PDMS to minimize the formation of new bubbles.
Place in the oven at 60 °C for at least 2 h to cure the PDMS.
Use a knife or razor blade to gently trace around the parameter of the culture device.
Carefully remove the mold from the cured PDMS.
Use a 4 mm biopsy punch to remove any PDMS from the bottom of the wells.
Cut the devices to fit on a glass coverslip.
Remove dust from the bottom side of the culture devices using tape.
Place clean glass coverslips and culture devices (bottom side up) on a hot plate at 135 °C for at least 15 min to remove moisture.
Use a corona plasma gun on high on both the glass coverslip and the bottom side of the device for 30 s, then quickly bond the treated surfaces together.
Gently apply pressure to ensure a good seal between the culture device and glass coverslip.
Weigh the lyo-µgels in a sterile hood and reconstitute in 84% of the final MAP volume of cell media based on the chosen wt% MAP.
Allow the µgels to swell for approximately 20 min.
Dissolve HA-Tet in cell media in 16% of the final MAP volume.
Aspirate the media from D1 mouse mesenchymal cells once they reach 70%-80% confluency.
Wash the cells with 1x PBS.
Add enough volume of 1% trypsin-EDTA to cover the surface of the tissue culture vessel.
Incubate at 37 °C for 1-3 min.
Quench the trypsinization by adding DMEM media supplemented with 1% pen-strep and 10% FBS at 2x the volume of trypsin-EDTA.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 100 x g for 5 min at room temperature to pellet the cells.
Aspirate the supernatant media and resuspend the cells in 1 mL DMEM media supplemented with 1% pen-strep and 10% FBS.
Transfer 20 µL of the cell suspension to a new microcentrifuge tube.
Add 20 µL trypan blue solution and mix well.
Use 20 µL of this mixture to count cells using either a hemocytometer or an automated cell counter with cell counting chamber slides.
Transfer the number of cells needed for seeding 10,000 cells/µL MAP to a new microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 100 x g for 5 min at room temperature to pellet the cells.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant media from the cell pellet without aspirating the cells.
Add µgels and crosslinker to the cell pellet with a displacement pipette.
Mix well with a displacement pipette.
Seed 10 µL of the mixture per well.
Pipette in a circular motion to evenly distribute the mixture in the well.
Allow the µgels to anneal at 37 °C in the cell incubator for 25 min.
Add cell media to fill the wells (~50 μL of media per well).
Maintain the 3D cultures at 37 °C.
Change media as needed, stabilizing the pipette tip along the ridge of the upper well.
Fix samples by removing the media and adding 50 μL of 4% paraformaldehyde per well for 30 min at room temperature.
Wash the samples 3x with 50 μL of 1x PBS or preferred buffer.
Image cells in MAP scaffolds on a confocal microscope using a 20x objective.
Obtain a Z-stack traversing 200-250 μm in the Z-direction with a step size of 2.5 μm.
Stain cells with DAPI diluted 1:1000 in 0.15% Triton-X in 1x PBS.
Stain cells with phalloidin-647 diluted 1:40 in 0.15% Triton-X in 1x PBS.
